title: Attestation-driven RBAC v2 and SIEM Export Playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook describes an attestation-driven RBAC v2 design and the associated audit/evidence export schema for SIEMs. Goal: provide deterministic, verifiable authorization decisions, compact evidence artifacts for compliance, and a migration/rollout plan with minimal application disruption.

Scope
- RBAC v2 = attribute-anchored role resolution + policy snapshots + attestation tokens
- Audit schema = canonical fields for downstream SIEMs and evidence automation
- Evidence pipeline = signing, storage, indexing, and export to SIEM/ELK/Splunk
- Migration/Rollout = discovery, canary, org roll, cutover, fallback

High-level design summary
1) Decision path: request -> attribute collection -> role resolution (RBAC-v2 engine) -> policy evaluation -> attestation emission -> response.
2) Attestation token: short-lived, signed blob that captures the attributes used, the policy snapshot id, and the decision. Stored in evidence store and referenced in audit logs.
3) Audit event: compact, structured record emitted synchronously for every decision and asynchronously for aggregated events (batch export).
4) SIEM mapping: we publish a stable export schema and per-SIEM adapter configs (Elasticsearch index mapping, Splunk sourcetype/kv mapping, Datadog logs pipeline).

Key concepts and primitives
- Attribute Anchors: canonical attribute names and normalization rules (user.email, user.uid, svc.account, caller_ip, source_vpc).
- Policy Snapshot ID: immutable hash of the resolved policy at evaluation time; stored to allow later replay/re-eval.
- Attestation Evidence Ref: a URI pointing to the signed attestation (e.g., s3://evidence-prod/2025/01/15/att-<id>.sig).
- Decision Outcome: allow | deny | conditional-allow (with recommended guardrails).

Audit log schema (recommended v2 canonical fields)
Fields (flat key/value pairs; all values are strings):
- event_ts: RFC3339 timestamp of decision
- request_id: unique identifier propagated through request path
- actor: canonical actor id (user:alice@example.com or service:payment-processor)
- actor_attributes: semicolon-delimited normalized attributes (e.g., email=alice@example.com;uid=1234)
- resource: resource canonical path (e.g., infra:dedicated-cluster:gpu-pool-7)
- action: requested action (e.g., inference:generate, model:deploy)
- decision: allow|deny|conditional
- policy_snapshot: <sha256-hash>
- policy_source: git://policies/main@rev or confluence id
- attestation_ref: URI to signed attestation blob
- evidence_refs: comma-separated list of additional evidence URIs (logs, config snapshots)
- latency_ms: numeric as string (end-to-end decision latency)
- server_node: internal node id that computed decision
- outcome_code: integer-safe code for downstream analytics
- reason: short free-text reason code or message
- signature_alg: e.g., ed25519
- signature_id: attestation signature id

Sample audit log (single-line JSON for SIEM ingestion):
{
  "event_ts": "2025-01-15T16:12:03Z",
  "request_id": "req-2476a9b0",
  "actor": "user:maya.chen@redwood.com",
  "actor_attributes": "email=maya.chen@redwood.com;uid=1123;roles=eng-security",
  "resource": "project:demo:model:bert-quant",
  "action": "model:serve",
  "decision": "allow",
  "policy_snapshot": "sha256:3f5b2e...",
  "policy_source": "git://policy-repo/main@b2c4f",
  "attestation_ref": "s3://rbac-evidence/prod/att-9c2f.sig",
  "evidence_refs": "s3://rbac-evidence/prod/req-2476a9b0/ctx.json",
  "latency_ms": "14",
  "server_node": "node-srv-17",
  "outcome_code": "200",
  "reason": "matched-role-engine:dataset-admin",
  "signature_alg": "ed25519",
  "signature_id": "sig-9c2f"
}

Evidence automation pipeline
- Ingest: RBAC engine writes attestation blob + signed artifact to evidence store (S3/GCS) with deterministic path layout
- Index: metadata service indexes attestation_ref, policy_snapshot, request_id, actor -> search index (Elasticsearch)
- Archive: longer-term retention copies to cold storage, retention controlled by tenant and compliance profiles
- Export: SIEM adapter fetches or receives events via push, transforms to SIEM canonical mapping, and writes to appropriate index/sourcetype.
- Verification: periodic background job replays archived attestations against frozen policy snapshot to detect drift.

SIEM export mapping rules (guidelines)
- Flatten actor attributes into discrete fields for SIEM (actor_email, actor_uid, actor_roles). If size grows, only send top-k attributes and include attestation_ref for full context.
- Provide a policy_snapshot field as a keyword/type that can be used as a join key with archived policy blobs.
- Use numeric latency_ms and outcome_code for dashboards and alerts.
- Include attestation_ref and evidence_refs as searchable keywords (not full-blobs) to keep ingestion cost low.
- For Splunk: use sourcetype=redwood:rbac and KV_MODE=auto; for Elasticsearch: provide index template rbac-logs-YYYY.MM.DD with mappings: event_ts: date, latency_ms: integer, policy_snapshot: keyword.

Security and privacy controls
- Sign all attestations (Ed25519 recommended) and store public keys in a key rotation service.
- Redact PII fields when tenant policy requires; the attestation_ref still points to the full blob accessible with proper entitlements.
- Encrypt evidence at rest and in transit; use per-tenant encryption keys where regulatory requirements demand.

Rollout plan (phases)
Phase 0 - Discovery (2 weeks)
- Inventory existing authorization checks across hosted API, dedicated, private planes.
- Map existing events to canonical action/resource names.
- Produce attribute normalization table.

Phase 1 - Pilot (4 weeks)
- Implement RBAC-v2 engine in a shadow mode on a single service (e.g., Console deployment flows).
- Emit audit_v2 events only (no enforcement).
- Wire SIEM adapter for a single tenant and validate mappings.
- Validate attestation blob generation and signing.

Phase 2 - Canary (6 weeks)
- Turn on enforcement for a small set of non-critical paths; monitor for false-denies and latency regressions.
- Run replay jobs to validate policy_snapshot correctness.
- Tighten observability: dashboards for error rate, denied-by-policy, attestation generation failures.

Phase 3 - Gradual ramp (6-12 weeks)
- Expand enforcement by team and tenant; require policy owners to attest for key resources prior to cutover.
- Launch evidence automation to SIEM for all canary tenants.

Phase 4 - Org wide cutover
- Complete migration for all tenants and drain legacy logs to archival.
- Publish final policy snapshot versioning and freeze rules for a rolling-window grace period.

Rollback and mitigations
- Provide an immediate global fallback toggle that converts enforcement to 'log-only' for a service domain.
- Implement auto-fail-open for critical control plane flows with alerting to oncall.

Operational runbook (checklist)
Pre-cutover checks:
- [ ] Attribute coverage >= 95% for targeted endpoints (see discovery sheet).
- [ ] SIEM index templates applied and ingest tested.
- [ ] Signing key rotation test completed.
- [ ] Evidence store lifecycle policy configured.
- [ ] Policy owners onboarded and policy_snapshot audit passes.
During cutover:
- [ ] Monitor denied-by-policy counts and open incident if >0.5% of requests for 5m rolling window.
- [ ] Monitor attestation generation failure rate and latency; alert at >=0.1% failures.
- [ ] Verify SIEM ingest for event_ts skew and dropped events.
Post-cutover:
- [ ] Run weekly policy replay against archived attestations for 8 weeks.
- [ ] Produce compliance report: percent decisions with attestations, avg latency, storage size.

KPIs and telemetry
- Percentage of authorization decisions with attestation_ref (target 100%)
- Attestation generation latency p50/p95/p99 (target p99 < 50ms for local decisions)
- Evidence store cost per 1M requests (baseline measurement)
- SIEM ingestion error rate

Open design questions (short-term)
- How granular should policy_snapshot be (per-policy-file vs whole-repo hash)? Recommendation: per-evaluation policy bundle hash for reproducibility.
- What is the canonical retention policy per tenant by compliance tier? Need legal input per region.
- Do we include raw attribute payload in SIEM for debugging? Default: no. Send only normalized keys + attestation_ref.

Appendix A: Example attestation blob (human readable form)
-- attestation-9c2f.json --
{
  "attestation_id": "att-9c2f",
  "issued_at": "2025-01-15T16:12:03Z",
  "request_id": "req-2476a9b0",
  "actor": "user:maya.chen@redwood.com",
  "attributes": "email=maya.chen@redwood.com;uid=1123;team=eng-security",
  "policy_snapshot": "sha256:3f5b2e...",
  "decision": "allow",
  "signature": "base64-ed25519-signature..."
}

Appendix B: Quick test harness for developers
- Local dev env sets RBAC_V2_MODE=shadow or enforce and RBAC_AUDIT_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9200/test-rbac
- Sample curl for trace: curl -H \"x-request-id: req-local-01\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer dev-token\" \"https://api.dev.redwood.internal/v1/models/serve\" -d '{\"model\":\"test\" }'
- Verify that attestation file appears in evidence store and that a single-line JSON audit event lands in your SIEM sink.

Notes and references
- Aligns with our principle of deterministic, replayable compliance artifacts.
- This playbook should be iterated alongside policy authoring and the platform signing key rotation cadence.
- Expected next steps: formalize per-tenant retention SLAs, finalize SIEM adapter configs for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic, and schedule pilot with Console team in Feb 2025.

Document history
- 2025-01-15: initial draft by Maya Chen
- 2025-01-22: added SIEM mapping details (Arjun)
